Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 12, verse 1:

﴿Alif, Lam, Ra﴾: I am Allah, the Most Merciful. ﴿These﴾: these are ﴿the verses of the Manifest Book﴾, which make clear the lawful and the unlawful and the rulings; meaning: the Qur'an.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 12, verse 2:

﴿Indeed, We have sent it down﴾, meaning: the Book, ﴿as an Arabic Qur'an﴾, in the language of the Arabs, ﴿so that you may understand﴾, that you may comprehend.

We relate to you the best of stories (﴿نحن نقصُّ عليك أحسن القصص﴾): We explain to you the best of explanation (نبيِّن لك أحسن البيان) ﴿by what We have revealed﴾ (بما أوحينا): by Our having made it known (بإيماننا) ﴿to you this Qur'an, and indeed you were before it among the unaware﴾ (﴿إليك هذا القرآن وإن كنت من قبله لمن الغافلين﴾): And you were not, before it was revealed to you, except among the unaware (وما كنتَ من قبل أن يُوحى إليك إلاَّ من الغافلين).

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 12, verse 4:

﴿When﴾ remember when ﴿Yusuf said to his father: "O my father, indeed I saw eleven stars, and the sun and the moon; I saw them prostrating to me."﴾ The verse continues. Yusuf (peace be upon him) saw this dream, and when he related it to his father, the father feared for him because of the envy of his brothers toward him, so he said:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 12, verse 5:

﴿O my son, do not relate your vision to your brothers, lest they plot against you a scheme.﴾ They will devise a way to bring about your destruction, because they do not know its interpretation.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 12, verse 6:

﴿And thus﴾ like what you have seen, ﴿your Lord will choose you﴾ He will select you and prefer you, ﴿and teach you the interpretation of events﴾ the interpretation of dreams, ﴿and complete His favour upon you﴾ with prophethood, ﴿and upon the family of Ya'qub﴾ meaning: those among them specially chosen for prophethood, ﴿just as He completed it upon your two forefathers before, Ibrahim and Ishaq. Indeed your Lord is All-Knowing﴾ where He places prophethood, ﴿All-Wise﴾ in His creation.

Surely there were in Joseph and his brothers ﴿signs﴾ (ayat), meaning lessons and wonders, in their news and their stories, ﴿for those who ask﴾, namely those who asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about that, and he informed them of it while he was unaware of it, having never read a book. So in that was the clearest proof of his truthfulness.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 12, verse 8:

﴿When they said﴾: meaning, the brothers of Yusuf: ﴿"Yusuf and his brother [are] more beloved to our father than we, though we are a [strong] group"﴾ (ʿuṣba: a group). ﴿"Indeed, our father is in clear error."﴾ He erred by favouring Yusuf and his brother over us. (ḍalāl: error, mistake.)

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 12, verse 9:

﴿Kill Joseph, or cast him out to some land﴾, a land far away from his father, ﴿so that your father's face will be turned wholly to you﴾, meaning he will give his full attention to you, ﴿and after that you will be a righteous people﴾, meaning you will repent afterward, and God, glory be to Him, will accept your repentance.

**Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 12, verse 10:**

﴿A speaker among them said﴾, and he was Yahudha (Judah), the eldest of his brothers: ﴿Do not kill Joseph, but cast him into the depths of the well﴾, into a dark place in the well that the gaze of onlookers cannot reach, ﴿and some of the travelers will pick him up﴾, passers-by on the road, ﴿if you are determined to act﴾, that is, to achieve what you intend by separating him from his father. So when they conferred among themselves about this and resolved to throw him into the well

They said to their father, ﴿What is wrong with you that you do not entrust us with Joseph?﴾ (meaning: why do you fear for him at our hands?) ﴿Indeed, we are sincere well-wishers toward him﴾ in mercy, kindness, and compassion.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 12, verse 12:

﴿Send him with us tomorrow﴾ to the desert ﴿to enjoy himself and play﴾, i.e., to roam and be active, ﴿and indeed we will be his guardians﴾ from everything you fear for him.

﴿He said, "It saddens me that you take him away"﴾. Your taking him away saddens me, because he would part from me, so I would not see him. ﴿"And I fear the wolf may eat him"﴾, for their land abounded in wolves. ﴿"While you are heedless of him"﴾, busy with your herding.
﴿They said, "If the wolf eats him while we are a band, then indeed we would be losers."﴾ A group in his presence. ﴿Then indeed we would be losers﴾: incapable (lu'ajizun).

﴿So when they took him away and agreed to put him into the bottom of the well﴾. And they resolved upon that. We revealed to Yusuf in the well, to strengthen his heart: "You will surely be told of your dream, and you will surely inform your brothers of this deed of theirs after this day," ﴿while they do not perceive﴾ that you are Yusuf, at the time you inform them.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 12, verse 17:

﴿They said, "O our father, indeed we went racing with one another﴾ running and sprinting, so that it might become clear which of us was swifter in running. ﴿And we left Joseph by our belongings﴾ our clothes. ﴿So the wolf devoured him. And you will not believe us﴾ you will not accept us as truthful, ﴿even if we are truthful﴾ in all things, because you have accused us regarding this matter."﴾

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 12, verse 18:

﴿And they brought his shirt with false blood on it.﴾ Because it was not his blood; it was only the blood of a young goat. ﴿He said﴾ Ya'qub, peace be upon him: ﴿Nay, but﴾ meaning: it is not as you say. ﴿Your souls have made a matter seem fair to you﴾ meaning: your souls have adorned for you ﴿a matter﴾ concerning him, other than what you describe. ﴿So patience is most fitting﴾ meaning: my affair is patience ﴿beautiful﴾, which is the patience that has no restlessness in it and no complaint. ﴿And Allah is the One whose help is sought against what you describe﴾ meaning: it is by Him that I seek help in bearing this matter.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 12, verse 19:

﴿And a caravan came﴾, a company travelling for journey, ﴿and they sent their water-drawer﴾, who is the one who goes to the water to draw it for the people, ﴿and he lowered his bucket﴾, he sent it down into the well, and Yusuf (peace be upon him) grasped the rope. The water-drawer informed them of him, and when he saw him ﴿he said: "Good news!"﴾, meaning: "O joy!" ﴿"This is a boy!"﴾ And they concealed him as merchandise. The water-drawer concealed him, and so did the merchants who were with him from among others. They said: "This is merchandise which some of the people of the water have entrusted to us for sale." ﴿And God is Knowing of what they do﴾ concerning Yusuf. When his brothers learned of that, they came to them and said: "This is a runaway slave of ours." They said to them: "Then sell him to us," and they sold him to them. This is His saying: ﴿and they sold him for a meagre price﴾, unlawful, because the price of a free person is unlawful, ﴿a few dirhams counted﴾, for twenty-two dirhams. ﴿And they were﴾, meaning his brothers, ﴿concerning him﴾, concerning Yusuf, ﴿among those who were indifferent﴾. They did not know his station with God, the Exalted, and his honour with Him.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 12, verse 21:

﴿And the one who bought him from Egypt said to his wife﴾. He was al-ʿAzīz, the minister (ṣāḥib) of the king of Egypt: ﴿Make his residence honourable﴾, that is, treat him well for the duration of his stay with us. ﴿Perhaps he will benefit us﴾, that is, he will suffice us, once he has reached maturity and understands matters, with some of our affairs. ﴿Or we may adopt him as a son﴾. Now he was impotent (ḥaṣūr) and could not father children. ﴿And thus﴾, just as We delivered him from being killed and from the well, ﴿We established Joseph in the land﴾, meaning the land of Egypt, until he attained what he attained. ﴿And that We may teach him the interpretation of events﴾. We did that in confirmation of His saying: ﴿And He will teach you the interpretation of events﴾. ﴿And Allah is dominant over His affair﴾, over what He wills of His decree; no one dominant can overpower His affair, and no disputant can nullify His will. ﴿But most of the people﴾, namely the polytheists and those who do not believe in predestination (qadar), ﴿do not know﴾ that the power of Allah is dominant and His will is executed.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 12, verse 22:

﴿And when he reached his full strength﴾ thirty years old, ﴿We gave him judgment and knowledge﴾ intellect and understanding. ﴿And thus﴾ like what We have described of Yusuf's instruction, ﴿We reward the good-doers﴾ those who are patient through calamities, as Yusuf (peace be upon him) was.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 12, verse 23:

﴿And she, in whose house he was, sought to seduce him from himself.﴾ Meaning: the wife of the ruler (al-ʿAzīz) asked him to have intercourse with her. ﴿And she closed the doors.﴾ That is: she closed them. ﴿And she said, "Come, [I am] yours."﴾ That is: come forward and approach. ﴿He said, "I seek refuge in Allah."﴾ I seek Allah's protection from doing this. ﴿Indeed, he is my lord.﴾ Indeed, the one who bought me is my master. ﴿He has made my residence good.﴾ He has bestowed his honor upon me, so I will not betray him regarding his wife. ﴿Indeed, the wrongdoers will not succeed.﴾ Those who commit fornication (al-zunat) will not be made happy.

**[Verse 24]** ﴿And she certainly desired him, and he would have desired her.﴾ She longed for him, and he longed for her. ﴿Had he not seen the proof of his Lord.﴾ That proof was that Ya'qub (peace be upon him) was shown to him, biting on his fingers, saying: "Will you do the deed of the wicked when you are written among the prophets?" So he felt shame before him. The answer to "had not" (law la) is omitted, meaning: "Had he not seen the proof of his Lord, he would have carried out what he intended." ﴿Thus﴾, that is, We showed him the proof, ﴿so that We might turn away from him evil﴾, which is betrayal by its companion, ﴿and immorality﴾, which is committing the grave sin of fornication. ﴿Indeed, he was among Our sincere servants﴾, those who made their religion sincerely for God, glorified is He.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 12, verse 25:

﴿And they both raced to the door.﴾ That was because Yusuf, peace be upon him, when he saw the proof (al-burhan), rose hastily toward the door, and the woman followed him, seeking to catch hold of him. She reached only the back of his shirt and tore it. They then found the woman's husband at the door. Then at that moment a stratagem (kayd) came to her, and she made her husband believe that the rushing and hastening toward the door had been from her, not from Yusuf. So ﴿she said, "What is the penalty for one who intended evil to your wife, except that he be imprisoned or suffer a painful punishment?"﴾ She meant fornication (al-zina). ﴿Except that he be imprisoned﴾: confined in prison. ﴿Or a painful punishment﴾: by beating. When she said that, Yusuf became angry and ﴿said, "It was she who sought to seduce me from myself," and a witness testified﴾, that is, a judge ruled and a clarifier clarified, ﴿from her own family﴾, and he was the paternal cousin of the woman. So he said: ﴿"If his shirt is torn from the front, then she has spoken the truth and he is among the liars."﴾

**Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 12, verse 28:**

﴿When he saw that his shirt was torn from behind﴾ From the judgment of the witness and his explanation, which necessitates inference for distinguishing the liar from the truthful. When the woman's husband saw Joseph's shirt torn from behind, ﴿he said, "Indeed, it is from your guile (women's guile)."﴾ That is: your saying, ﴿"What is the recompense for one who intended evil against your family...?"﴾ the verse.

O Joseph, turn away from this matter, do not mention it. And ask forgiveness for your sin, for you were indeed among the sinners (al-khati'in), the guilty.

Then what had passed between them spread throughout the city of Egypt, until the women talked about it and delved into it, and this is His saying:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 12, verse 30:

﴿And women said in the city, "The wife of the chief minister is seeking to seduce her young slave from himself. He has captivated her heart with love; indeed, we see her in clear error."﴾

Her young slave (ghulamuha). He has entered into the innermost part of her heart with his love (qad shaghafaha hubban), and the shaghaf is the place of blood that lies inside the heart. ﴿Indeed, we see her in clear error﴾ (fi dalal), that is, astray from the path of right guidance, through her love for him.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 12, verse 31:

﴿Then when she heard﴾ of the al-Aziz's wife ﴿of their scheming﴾ their remark, and it was called scheming because they intended by this remark that she show them Yusuf, so that her excuse for loving him would be established if they saw his beauty; and they were desirous of that, because Yusuf had been described to them as beautiful. ﴿She sent to them﴾ inviting them ﴿and prepared for them a banquet﴾ and made ready ﴿for them a reclining-cushion﴾ food to be cut with a knife; it was said: it was the citron. ﴿And she gave each one of them a knife﴾ and handed out ﴿and said﴾ to Yusuf: ﴿Go out to them.﴾ ﴿Then when they saw him, they were struck with awe of him﴾ they were amazed by him, his affair overwhelmed them and they were stunned, ﴿and they cut their hands﴾ they gashed them with the knives, and they did not feel the pain because their hearts were occupied with Yusuf. ﴿And they said: Far is God from imperfection!﴾ Yusuf is too far removed from being a mere human; ﴿This is not﴾ this is not ﴿but a noble angel.﴾ When the al-Aziz's wife saw that, she said:

That is the one you blamed me for. (Al-Wahidi's gloss:) regarding his love and her infatuation with him. Then she confessed to them what she had done, and said: ﴿And I did seek to seduce him, but he refused.﴾ He resisted and refused, and she threatened him with prison, saying: ﴿And if he does not do what I command him, he will certainly be imprisoned and will be of the debased.﴾ Then they urged him to obey her, and said to him: "You are the wrongdoer, and she is the wronged," so Yusuf said:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 12, verse 33:

﴿My Lord, prison is dearer to me than what they invite me to,﴾ [i.e., to disobedience to You] ﴿and unless You turn away their scheming from me, I might incline toward them﴾ [the scheming of all the women] ﴿and become one of the ignorant﴾ [the sinners].

So his Lord answered him and turned away from him their scheming. (Yusuf's prayer was answered) so that he did not fall into anything they were demanding of him. "Indeed, He is the All-Hearing" of his supplication, "the All-Knowing" of what he feared of sin.

Then it occurred to them, after they had seen the signs (the signs of Yusuf's innocence), that they should imprison him for a time. [Qur'an 12:35]

That is: al-Aziz and his companions, after they had seen the signs of Yusuf's innocence, decided to imprison him for a period. The reason was that the woman said: "This slave has disgraced me among the people; he will tell them that I solicited him. So imprison him until this talk ends." This is His saying: "for a time," meaning until the blame ceases.

And there entered the prison with him two young men. They were two servants of the great king. It was reported to him that the one in charge of his food intended to poison him, and that his cupbearer had colluded with him in this, so he had them both put in prison. They saw Joseph interpreting dreams, and said: "Let us test this Hebrew servant." So they dreamt, though neither of them had actually seen anything; this is his saying: ﴿One of them said﴾, namely the cupbearer: ﴿"Indeed, I see myself pressing wine."﴾ That is, grapes. The one in charge of the food said: ﴿"Indeed, I see myself carrying bread upon my head."﴾ I saw as if there was bread on my head ﴿"of which the birds eat."﴾ Then birds of prey were pecking at it. ﴿"Inform us of its interpretation."﴾ That is, tell us the explanation of the dream. ﴿"Indeed, we see you to be among the doers of good."﴾ You are one who favors good and does beautiful deeds. So Joseph, peace be upon him, turned away from answering their question, and first showed them that he knew the interpretation of the dream, and said:

"Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 12, verse 37:

﴿The food that is provided to you both will not come to you⁠—﴾ you both will eat from it in your sleep ﴿except that I will inform you of its interpretation⁠﴾ while awake ﴿before it comes to you.﴾ The interpretation. ﴿That is from what my Lord has taught me.⁠﴾ That is: I am not informing you by way of soothsaying (takahhun) and astrology (tanajjum); rather, that is by revelation from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and by knowledge. Then he informed about his faith and his avoidance of disbelief with the rest of the verse."

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 12, verse 38:

And His saying: ﴿It is not for us to associate anything with Allah﴾ meaning: Allah, glory be to Him, has protected us from associating anything with Him. ﴿This is of the bounty of Allah upon us﴾, that is: our following of faith is by Allah's grace and His favour upon us. ﴿And upon mankind﴾, and upon whomever Allah has protected from shirk so that he follows His religion. ﴿But most of mankind do not give thanks﴾ for the blessing of Allah in His Oneness and in belief in His messengers. Then he (Yusuf) called them both to faith, saying:

O my two fellow prisoners! Are scattered lords better, or Allah, the One, the Subduer?

(Here "scattered lords" means the idols.) "Better" here means greater in the quality of praise. "The One, the Subduer" is He who overpowers everything.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 12, verse 40:

﴿What you worship besides Him﴾ — you two and those who are in a state like yours — besides Allah, ﴿are but names﴾ with no meanings behind them, ﴿which you have named﴾ ﴿Judgment belongs only to Allah﴾ — the authority of command and prohibition belongs only to Allah ﴿That is the upright religion﴾ — the straight one, ﴿but most of the people do not know﴾ — [the reward for the obedient and the punishment for the disobedient]. Then he mentioned the interpretation of their dream with his words:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 12, verse 41:

﴿O my two companions of the prison, as for one of you, he will give his lord drink of wine; and as for the other, he will be crucified, and the birds will eat from his head.﴾ They said: "We did not see anything." He said: ﴿The matter has been decided about which you both inquire.﴾ Meaning: what I have interpreted for you will come to pass upon you both, whether you spoke truthfully or lied.

Yusuf said to the one whom he thought (ẓanna) would be saved (ʿilm) from the two of them, who was the cupbearer: ﴿Mention me before your lord.﴾ That is, mention me to the king, your master, and tell him: Indeed there is in the prison a youth imprisoned unjustly. ﴿But Satan caused him to forget the remembrance of his lord.﴾ Satan made Yusuf forget to seek help from his Lord, and he put into his heart the seeking of help from the king. So he was punished by ﴿remaining in the prison for several years﴾, seven years. Then, when his release drew near and Allah willed his deliverance, the king saw a dream, and it is his saying:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 12, verse 43:

﴿And the king said, "Indeed, I see...﴾ the verse, when he consulted them about it.

﴿They said, "A confusion of dreams"﴾ — confused dreams with no interpretation (ta'wil) according to us. ﴿And we are not, of the interpretation of dreams, learned﴾ — they acknowledged their inability to interpret them.

And the one of the two who was saved from them said, ﴿And the one who was saved of the two said﴾, namely the cupbearer, ﴿and he remembered after a period﴾, and he recalled the matter of Yusuf after a long time of days, ﴿I will inform you of its interpretation, so send me forth﴾. So he was sent, and he came to Yusuf and said:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 12, verse 46:

﴿Yusuf﴾ meaning: O Yusuf, ﴿O truthful one (al-siddiq)﴾, the one who is very truthful. And his saying ﴿that I may return to the people﴾ means: the companions of the king, ﴿that they may know﴾ the interpretation of the king's dream from your side.

﴿He said, "You shall sow"﴾, i.e., sow ﴿for seven years in succession﴾, consecutively. These seven years are the interpretation (ta'wil) of the fat cows. ﴿What you reap﴾ of what you have sown, ﴿leave it in its ears﴾, because that preserves it better and keeps it further from spoiling, ﴿except for a little which you eat﴾, for you will thresh it.

Then after that will come seven hard years, which will consume what you have stored up for them, except a little of what you have preserved.

Those are seven years of drought and hardship, and this is the interpretation of the lean cows. "Will consume" means they will destroy and make away with it. "What you have stored up for them" means the grain. "Except a little of what you store away" means what you guard and keep in reserve.

Then after that there will come a year in which the people will be given rain and in which they will press (their produce).

They will receive rain and the land will become fertile, so that they press sesame for oil, grapes for wine, and olives for oil. So the messenger returned to the king with the interpretation of the dream, and the king recognised that this was a correct interpretation, and said:
